content:
Every integer \(n \ge 2\) is either prime or composite, so the only number from 1 to 1000 that is neither prime nor composite is \(1\). But \(1=1^2\) is a perfect square, so it is also excluded.

Thus there are 0 qualifying numbers, so the probability is

\[
\frac{0}{1000}=0.
\]

\boxed{0}
